The rationale: The critical-path tail layers (norm2, res2, GeLU, res1) have 50-59% memory time and 40-56% communication time. Increasing DRAM BW from 64 to 128 directly reduces the memory component of these layers, which should lower the critical end time and potentially reduce memory energy. The IO cost is only 7.9% of total MC, so the MC increase from doubling DRAM BW should be modest. The compute-bound FFN1 layers (68.4% of time) are unaffected by DRAM BW, but the critical-path tail improvement could reduce total latency and improve core utilization. This is a cost-effective move compared to increasing chiplet count (which would increase OS cost by 39.4%) or NoP BW (which historically failed on 16 chiplets). DRAM BW increase from 64 to 128 directly targets the memory component of the critical-path tail with modest MC impact (IO is only 7.9% of total cost). Historical NoP increase failed on 16 chiplets, and chiplet count increase would significantly increase OS cost (39.4%). The materialized candidate is ready for evaluation."}
